transcript:
Meeting Header: 2025-12-03T15:00 PST | Duration: ~47 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood DevAdv); Samantha Ortiz, Liam Patel, Tara Nguyen (Nebula Commerce)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood client libraries for Python and TypeScript, authentication options (API keys vs SSO), env setup for local dev and CI, demo of the Console for routing and Optimize suggestions, and next steps for a pairing session and benchmark. Some audio glitches mid-call; a few words mis-transcribed.

Topics: client-lib install, API key patterns, SSO/SAML notes, environment variables and .env best practices, TS types for responses, streaming vs non-streaming usage, Redwood Console routes, Optimize suggestions for batching and caching, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh, really quickintro, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE for EMEA and APAC, with Priya and Marcus on the call.
00:18 Samantha Ortiz: Thanks, Alex. We (laugh) we got a small group from Nebula — I'm Sam, engineering manager. Liam and Tara are here — Liam will be doing the integration, Tara is looking at security.
00:34 Priya Nair: Great, quick agenda — 1) show client libs in Python and TS, 2) auth patterns and env setup, 3) Console demo (routes + Optimize suggestions), 4) Q&A + next steps. Sound good?
00:45 Liam Patel: Yep, sounds good. We're hoping to get a working quickstart by end of next week.
00:52 Marcus Lee: I'll jump in with some code snippets and show a couple of gotchas we see in front-end bundlers and serverless.
01:05 Tara Nguyen: Also want to surface SOC2 and KMS questions early — we handle payment-adjacent data and need to know about encryption and audit logs.

01:18 Alex Chen: Absolutely, Tara — we'll cover the KMS/keys and audit logs in Console and the Private options too. Quick reminder, this is a walkthrough not a full POC scoping session but we'll capture action items.

02:05 --- Demo: Python quickstart ---
02:10 Priya Nair: Ok going to share screen, first Python. Typical install: pip install redwood-inference (note: package name may appear as redwood-client in some older docs). Example quickstart:
02:28 [02:28] Priya Nair: from redwood import RedwoodClient
02:34 [02:34] Priya Nair: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
02:40 [02:40] Priya Nair: resp = client.generate("summarize: ...")
02:46 Liam Patel: How do you recommend storing the key in CI?
02:50 Priya Nair: We generally use secrets manager and set REDWOOD_API_KEY in the CI environment. For local dev we recommend a .env but not checked into repo. We also support short-lived tokens via our SSO integration for users who want per-user auth.
03:15 Samantha Ortiz: Is there a role-based SDK token support? We have multiple services calling the API on different privileges.
03:23 Alex Chen: Great question. We support token scoping — you can mint tokens with scopes (read/generate/admin) via the Console or via an API for automations. Note: token naming in some older docs is inconsistent, sometimes called "service tokens" or "deploy tokens".

04:00 --- TypeScript quickstart ---
04:05 Marcus Lee: For TypeScript, npm i @redwood/inference or yarn add @redwood/inference. Example:
04:15 Marcus Lee: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
04:20 Marcus Lee: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
04:28 Marcus Lee: client.chat.stream("Explain the checkout flow") .on('data', chunk => { /* handle streaming chunk */ })
04:38 Liam Patel: Any notes for bundlers? We're using Vite and serverless functions.
04:43 Marcus Lee: If you're calling from browser, don't put API key in client bundle — use a backend proxy or short-lived tokens. For serverless, ensure you use the Node-specific build, and watch for polyfills — some users inadvertently pull in big crypto libs.

05:20 Tara Nguyen: Can you briefly explain SSO flow — SAML vs OIDC? We use Okta.
05:28 Alex Chen: We integrate with SAML SSO and OIDC; for Okta OIDC it's straightforward. For SAML the Console guides you through metadata exchange. When SSO is enabled, tokens are minted per user and can be tied to RBAC. The team must enable SSO in the org settings; for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with customer IAP as well.

06:05 Samantha Ortiz: About Private deployment — we have strict data residency EU-first. Is that covered?
06:12 Priya Nair: Yes, Private supports EU-only data planes, and Dedicated reserved pools can be pinned to regions. We'll note that in the action items.

06:40 --- Environment variables and .env patterns ---
06:45 Marcus Lee: Quick best practice: REDWOOD_API_KEY for service tokens; REDWOOD_ORG_ID if you want to select a tenant; REDWOOD_MODEL to pin a model for local dev. In CI, use your secrets vault and rotate keys monthly.
07:10 Liam Patel: Are there SDK helpers for refreshing short-lived tokens?
07:14 Priya Nair: Yes, there are refresh helpers in the SDK and examples in the repo. We also provide a CLI helper to mint ephemeral tokens for dev. Might be in the "redwood-cli" package.

08:00 --- Console demo: routes, models, and Optimize ---
08:05 Alex Chen: Switching to Console; this is where you can create routes, pin model versions, and view Optimize suggestions.
08:22 [08:22] Alex Chen: Here we have an example route that uses a lower-cost quantized model during non-critical workflows and a higher-quality model for checkout. You can set automatic fallback policies if latency SLOs are missed.
08:40 Samantha Ortiz: How does Optimize recommend batching? We have variable payload sizes.
08:46 Priya Nair: Optimize analyzes token distributions and suggests batching and prefix caching. For e.g., it may recommend a 128-token prefix cache for your common chat headers and 4-concurrent batching for requests under 300 tokens. It's a heuristic plus simulated cost savings.
09:10 Liam Patel: Is there an API to pull those suggestions? We want them in our infra dashboard.
09:15 Priya Nair: Yes — Optimize exposes suggestions as JSON via the Console API, you can pull and incorporate into your deploy pipeline.

10:00 --- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs ---
10:05 Marcus Lee: Streaming reduces time-to-first-byte but can increase complexity in front-end assembly and monitoring. Batching reduces total tokens consumed but may add latency. For Nebula checkout flows we usually recommend streaming for interactive UI and non-streaming for offline batch summarization.
10:40 Samantha Ortiz: Latency vs cost: what are typical ballparks?
10:44 Alex Chen: Depends on model and quantization — a quantized LLaMA-family variant on Dedicated might be 2-5x cheaper than a full fp16 hosted option, but latency can vary. We'll provide a benchmark matrix.

11:20 --- Security and compliance ---
11:25 Tara Nguyen: Audit logs — do they show token usage down to request-level?
11:30 Alex Chen: Console audit logs keep request metadata (timestamp, route, model, tokens) and you can export to your SIEM. For Private deployments we support forwarding to customer SIEM via secure logs. KMS: we support customer-managed keys for encrypting stored artifacts.
11:48 Tara Nguyen: Is PII stripped by default?
11:52 Priya Nair: No automatic stripping by default; we recommend using our data-handling middleware and redaction hooks. There's also an optional pre-processor step in the SDK to hash or redact fields.

12:30 --- Live coding: small end-to-end example ---
12:35 Marcus Lee: I'm going to walk through a small Node lambda example. Note: some transcripts earlier show "KV cash" — that's actually KV cache, the key-value cache.
12:48 [12:48] Marcus Lee: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
12:55 Marcus Lee: await client.generate({ model: 'rw-v1-small', input: 'Summarize latest order' })
13:05 Liam Patel: If we pin rw-v1-small, and later upgrade, can we roll back?
13:09 Priya Nair: Yes, Console supports versioned model rollouts and canary percentages. You can also set automatic fallback to a previous variant on quality regressions.

14:00 --- Common gotchas ---
14:05 Marcus Lee: Watch for: bundling API keys into front-end; polyfills for serverless; threading limits in certain Node runtimes causing KV cache lockups (rare); and mismatched TypeScript types if you rely on auto-generated types — stay on the same SDK minor.
14:35 Liam Patel: Are there webhooks for async task completions?
14:40 Priya Nair: Yes, you can configure async callbacks for longer-running jobs.

15:00 --- Benchmarking and POC notes ---
15:05 Alex Chen: For the benchmark, we'll need sample payloads and expected QPS. Priya will run against Hosted and Dedicated variants and return a matrix of latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, and failure rate.
15:22 Samantha Ortiz: Our expected traffic during checkout peaks ~200 RPS; baseline is about 60-80ms p95 today.
15:32 Alex Chen: Good context — that helps sizing Dedicated pools.

16:10 --- Questions from Tara about legal/procurement ---
16:15 Tara Nguyen: Contractually, we need data processing addendum and SOC2 report. Where do we find them?
16:20 Alex Chen: We'll share the security package link (I'll send with the follow-up). For Dedicated and Private we have enterprise contracts.

17:00 --- Small audio glitch, transcription note ---
17:05 [17:05] Speaker 4: (garbled)
17:12 Alex Chen: Sorry about that — re-iterating KMS support, audit logs, and SIEM export.

18:00 --- Deep-dive note on Optimize suggestions ---
18:05 Priya Nair: Optimize correlates traffic shape to model profiles and suggests quantization and batching. For example, it might say: 'Switch to q4_0 variant for non-critical paths and enable prefix KV cache for repeated user prompts' which reduced token consumption by ~28% in a previous retail customer.

19:10 Samantha Ortiz: Do you have examples for how to wire Optimize suggestions into CI?
19:16 Priya Nair: Yes, example: Fetch suggestions via Console API, generate a config diff, and apply via Terraform or our deployment API. We can share a sample GitHub Actions workflow.

20:00 --- Pricing and Dedicated commitments ---
20:05 Alex Chen: Pricing varies — hosted is usage-based per token; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. I'll send a tailored pricing sheet. Important to note: Dedicated reduces per-token cost but has commitment windows.
20:30 Liam Patel: If we start hosted and then move to Dedicated, how disruptive is that?
20:34 Alex Chen: We provide routing and model variant compatibility so that you can migrate with near-zero code change — usually it's rerouting in Console or switching an env var.

21:10 --- Live troubleshooting — local .env example ---
21:15 Marcus Lee: Example .env file to not commit:
21:20 [21:20] Marcus Lee: REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
21:24 Marcus Lee: REDWOOD_ORG_ID=org_yyy
21:27 Marcus Lee: REDWOOD_DEFAULT_MODEL=rw-v1-small
21:32 Liam Patel: Should we include region hints in the env var?
21:36 Priya Nair: You can set REDWOOD_REGION=eu-west-1 for region pinning if you're in Private or Dedicated. For hosted, region selection is automatic but you can set a preferred region for routing.

22:10 --- Short discussion on observability ---
22:15 Alex Chen: Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, plus per-route traces. We also offer tracing hooks to push to Zipkin or Datadog.
22:32 Samantha Ortiz: Will that show prompt/response content? We have PII concerns.
22:38 Alex Chen: Content redaction is configurable — logs can omit prompt text and only show metadata.

23:00 --- Q&A rapid fire ---
23:05 Liam Patel: Type-safety for responses?
23:08 Marcus Lee: We expose TypeScript generics and you can pass in expected schemas; also support function-calling-like structured outputs.
23:20 Samantha Ortiz: Any rate limits on the hosted tier?
23:24 Alex Chen: Yes, per-account rate limits; Dedicated gives you more predictable throughput and burst options.

24:10 --- Wrap and next steps recap ---
24:15 Alex Chen: Recap — we'll send: 1) quickstart repo links for Python and TS, 2) tailored pricing and Dedicated options, 3) security package + SOC2, 4) schedule pairing session.
24:34 Samantha Ortiz: Great — Sam here will coordinate the pairing session date.
24:40 Tara Nguyen: We'll also send our compliance checklist.
24:44 Alex Chen: Awesome. Priya, anything to add?
24:48 Priya Nair: I'll follow up with sample benchmark plan and ask for sample payloads.
24:55 Marcus Lee: I'll drop a note about common bundler gotchas and a small serverless example repo.
